title: IT Consultant Roadmap
summary: Build technical breadth first, then develop requirements analysis, solution design, project delivery, client communication and business-domain expertise.

facts.Timeline assumption: Four-year B.Tech/B.E. beginning in 2026 and ending around 2030. The roadmap assumes a technical consulting route rather than a purely management-focused consulting route.

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: Programming, databases, cloud, systems analysis, requirements gathering, presentations, project work and internship experience.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Enterprise applications, cloud transformation, cybersecurity, data/AI, ERP/CRM or technology strategy.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Solution architecture, programme delivery, client ownership, business-case development and consulting leadership.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Technology strategy, enterprise architecture, AI transformation, risk, governance and executive advisory work.

blocks.text: Four-year honours variant

If you take the four-year honours/research variant, use the additional year for a substantial enterprise/technology project, research, advanced cloud/data/security work or a consulting-oriented capstone. Build evidence of problem definition, solution evaluation and measurable outcomes.

blocks.label: Evolve and stay relevant, 2035–2046
blocks.text: Develop from solving individual technical problems to defining business problems, evaluating alternatives, designing solutions and managing implementation. Add industry knowledge—such as banking, healthcare, telecom, retail or manufacturing—to make your technical skills more useful in consulting engagements.

blocks.label: Career progression

blocks.text: These are typical stages, not guaranteed promotion dates.
PhD routes

Move toward technology strategy, enterprise architecture, transformation programmes or specialist advisory work. Maintain enough technical depth to evaluate architectures and implementation risks, while developing stronger financial, operational, regulatory and industry knowledge.
